No. The method did not detect any tree-cover loss event of 0.5 ha or more on ASSET-D (311.2 ha) between 2021-01-01 and 2025-12-31. This is based on Hansen Global Forest Change (GFC-2025-v1.13), with valid observations covering 100% of the property and data through 2025. The JRC 2020 map shows 285.6 ha of forest (about 91.8% of the property) at the baseline.

Limits to keep in mind:
- Smaller changes (under 0.5 ha), changes at edges, or changes narrower than the 30 m pixels could be missed, so this doesn't prove that no change happened at all.
- This is not a regulatory or compliance finding, so it doesn't say the property is EUDR compliant or deforestation-free.
- It says nothing about periods outside 2021–2025.

The evidence is current as of 2026-11-12.
